Company: Ledgerly Inc.

US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.

Rules that APPLY:
- Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
- OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
- CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps
- Consumer data privacy / GLBA, open banking (1033)
- FTC consumer protection that touches payment apps
- Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
- Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
- CFTC derivatives market rules (DCMs, swaps)
- Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
- Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually

[2026-22809] Proposed Rule — Treasury Department; Financial Crimes Enforcement Network
Title: Threshold for the Requirement To Collect, Retain, and Transmit Information on Funds Transfers and Transmittals of Funds That Begin or End Outside the United States, and Clarification of the Requirement To Collect, Retain, and Transmit Information on Transactions Involving Convertible Virtual Currencies and Digital Assets With Legal Tender Status; Withdrawal
Action: Proposed rule; withdrawal.
Abstract: FinCEN and the Board (collectively, the "Agencies") are withdrawing the joint notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) published on October 27, 2020, that proposed modifying the threshold in the Agencies' rules implementing the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) requiring financial institutions to collect and retain information on certain funds transfers and transmittals of funds. The NPRM would have reduced this threshold from $3,000 to $250 for funds transfers and transmittals of funds that begin or end outside the United States. FinCEN additionally proposed reducing from $3,000 to $250 the threshold in FinCEN's rule requiring financial institutions to transmit to other financial institutions in the payment chain information on funds transfers and transmittals of funds that begin or end outside the United States. The NPRM also would have clarified the meaning of "money" as used in the Agencies' rules to specify that the rules apply to domestic and cross-border transactions involving convertible virtual currency (CVC) and digital assets that have legal tender status to a recipient. The Agencies will not take further action on this NPRM.

# Regulatory triage — Ledgerly Inc.
Window 2026-11-09 → 2026-11-13 · as of 2026-11-13 · 7 items

## Critical (1)

- **Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of Funds Involving MEXC Global** [Federal Register]
  - Direct Priya Shah to block all MEXC Global-linked transmittals and addresses in wallet and cross-border flows, since the FinCEN prohibition makes violations a direct liability.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-10 (effective, FR field ✓) · Owner: Priya Shah (BSA Officer) · Areas: aml-bsa, crypto, sanctions
  - 91 FR 72420 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22962/imposition-of-special-measure-prohibiting-the-transmittal-of-funds-involving-mexc-global

## High (4)

- **Publication of Iran-Related Web General Licenses EE and FF** [Federal Register]
  - Have Marcus Lee confirm Iran General Licenses EE and FF are reflected in screening and remittance controls, since they have been in effect for over a month.
  - Deadline: 2026-10-08 (effective, quoted ✓) · Owner: Marcus Lee (Sanctions) · Areas: sanctions
  - 91 FR 73140 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/13/2026-23197/publication-of-iran-related-web-general-licenses-ee-and-ff
- **Publication of Iran-Related Web General License W** [Federal Register]
  - Have Marcus Lee review Iran-related General License W against current blocking rules and decide whether any screening or payment handling needs adjusting.
  - Deadline: none found · Owner: Marcus Lee (Sanctions) · Areas: sanctions
  - 91 FR 73142 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/13/2026-23193/publication-of-iran-related-web-general-license-w
- **Publication of a Cuba Sanctions Regulations Web General License** [Federal Register]
  - Have Marcus Lee assess Cuba General License 1 against remittance and payment controls, and update escalation procedures only where the authorization applies to Ledgerly flows.
  - Deadline: none found · Owner: Marcus Lee (Sanctions) · Areas: sanctions
  - 91 FR 73139 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/13/2026-23195/publication-of-a-cuba-sanctions-regulations-web-general-license
- **Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 55F and 115D** [Federal Register]
  - Have Marcus Lee review Russia General Licenses 55F and 115D, and adjust screening rules and release procedures if any authorized dealings touch Ledgerly transactions.
  - Deadline: none found · Owner: Marcus Lee (Sanctions) · Areas: sanctions
  - 91 FR 73140 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/13/2026-23196/publication-of-russian-harmful-foreign-activities-sanctions-regulations-web-general-licenses-55f-and
